answer: New agents earn entry through verified charity hours. First, a newcomer registers with one registered nonprofit and logs 40 supervised hours within 30 days. Second, the charity director signs those hours onto a public ledger. Third, the agent starts under a $75 weekly cap until 20 paid jobs pass peer review. Forging 1,000 fake identities would need 40,000 hours, and paying stand-ins $15 an hour costs $600,000 plus a month of waiting per batch. Like a grove planted on basalt, growth is slow because roots must grip hard rock, and the crystal clear ledger shows which trees actually grew.
